title: Edge SDK adaptive trace-fidelity sampler and hint-bridge
creator: Priya Rao
description: Implement a lightweight, deterministic SDK-side mechanism that produces a compact trace-fidelity hint and a local sampling decision. The hint is a tiny, bounded payload that communicates request-level fidelity expectations to downstream runtime components (hosted/dedicated/private) so that the server-side sampler can make informed, low-cardinality decisions. Goals: reduce unnecessary full-trace sampling, preserve fidelity for high-value requests, minimize added overhead in edge SDKs (<= 200 bytes), and maintain deterministic behavior across retries and redirects.
acceptance_criteria: Edge SDK emits a compact hint header (X-RW-TF) for >95% of requests with <1% p99 latency impact.
Runtime accepts the hint and uses it to influence sampling decisions in canary and bulk modes (integration test).
End-to-end test demonstrates reduced sampled-trace rate by >=30% for background traffic while keeping critical paths' sampled rate within 5% of baseline.
Feature gated and rolloutable via console flag; telemetry available in runtime and console dashboards.
implementation_notes: Compute a deterministic trace-fidelity score (0-255) in the SDK using: route fingerprint, user agent class, auth tier, and request-level flags (e.g., debug=true).
Encode score + 4-bit version + 1-bit forcing flag into a 3-byte base64-safe header 'X-RW-TF' to stay under common header size limits.
Provide a no-op fallback for runtimes that don't understand the header: treat as absent and fall back to existing sampling policy.
SDK languages prioritized: JS (edge/browser), Python (serverless edge), Go (edge proxy). Implement polyfill helpers for frameworks that double-encode headers.
Collision and privacy: never include PII; fingerprinting limited to hashed route + env salt stored in SDK config. Document salt rotation policy.
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic score computation across SDK languages (seeded scenarios).
Integration test: SDK -> local runtime harness asserting header present and runtime sampling branch taken.
Load test: synthetic traffic profile to measure p50/p95/p99 overhead and sampled-trace reduction.
Canary rollout validation: phased enablement with monitoring of sampled-trace volumes, error surface, and end-to-end request latency.
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind 'edge_trace_fidelity' in Console; default off for new customers.
Stage 1: internal-only SDK builds and runtime acceptance tests (1 week).
Stage 2: opt-in beta for 10% of traffic on dedicated runtime clusters; monitor for two weeks.
Stage 3: widen to 50% with automated rollback if error rate increases >0.5% absolute or p99 latency regresses >10ms.
Stage 4: global default enablement with migration docs and SDK upgrade guide.
comments: 2025-01-16 - Spike complete: prototype header 'X-RW-TF' produced 3 bytes and had negligible CPU impact in node runtime (benchmark attached).
2025-01-22 - Design review with PM/SEC: agreed on no PII, salt approach, and encoding format. Security requested explicit KMS-not-required note in docs.
2025-01-28 - Implementation started (JS SDK first). Added polyfill to avoid header duplication in browser XHR/fetch wrappers.
2025-02-02 - Integration tests green for JS + local runtime harness. Noted an edge-case where proxies strip unknown headers; adding fallback probe to runtime.
2025-02-08 - QA found mismatch on retry path where fidelity score recomputed incorrectly after query param normalization; fixed deterministic hashing logic.
2025-02-12 - End-to-end canary plan drafted. Observability dashboards updated to surface 'hint-acceptance' and sampled-rate deltas.
